mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400 units, indicating strengthening demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1400, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing borrowing costs and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, always-on.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200k in a month, the combined signal of a strong labor market drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average, signaling supply chain resilience, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 55% of instances when INDPRO > 6-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: a high and rising GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong aggregate demand, consistently driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP and stock market correlation
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.035 over any 2.5-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 6% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate exceeds 3%, the combined signal of tightening monetary policy and inflation concerns drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 45% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% without a corresponding increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth signals labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market imbalances and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: a low and stable industrial production (INDPRO) growth rate, indicating supply chain stability, consistently drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
